summary: Daniel Dockery argues that Spider-Man is the ideal superhero for Thanksgiving because his relatable loneliness, money troubles and struggle for balance mirror the holiday's emphasis on shared meals and mutual support. He examines the chaotic Thanksgiving scene in the 2002 Spider-Man film and the warmer dinner in The Spectacular Spider-Man's first season finale. He also notes Spider-Man's real-world tie to the holiday as the only Marvel character with a balloon in the Macy's Thanksgiving Parade.
one_line: Spider-Man's relatable struggles and loneliness make him the perfect Thanksgiving superhero, as shown in the 2002 film, The Spectacular Spider-Man, and the Macy's parade.
key_facts: Marvel built its comic book revolution on making colorful superheroes relatable, in contrast to DC heroes of the mid 20th century, described as 'square-jawed Sunday school teachers'.
Peter Parker is often the most financially strapped among his Avengers buddies, and frequently the loneliest.
Feelings of loneliness spike during the holidays, so late November can make people feel more like Peter Parker.

In the 2002 Spider-Man film's Thanksgiving dinner, Norman Osborn sticks his fingers into Aunt May's sweet-potato casserole, figures out Spider-Man's secret identity, and gives Harry a sexist diatribe, leaving Harry and Mary Jane at odds.
In that 2002 scene, Peter, who has just lost his Uncle Ben, arrives with cranberry sauce and enjoys a moment of respite in a room where he knows he's loved.
Aunt May and Peter end up with a ton of leftovers after everyone else storms out of the 2002 film's dinner.
The first season of The Spectacular Spider-Man ends with Eddie Brock having become Venom and threatening everyone Peter holds dear, just after Peter was infected by the symbiote.
In The Spectacular Spider-Man finale, Peter cooks Thanksgiving dinner alone and mostly ruins the kitchen, but Gwen Stacy, her father, Aunt May and her doctor help out.
The Spectacular Spider-Man episode ends with a pleasant dinner, Aunt May revealing she is publishing a cookbook, and Peter getting a kiss from Gwen on his porch.
Spider-Man is the only Marvel character to rate a balloon in the Macy's Thanksgiving Parade.
The Spider-Man balloon was inflated to 80 feet and pulled through the Upper West Side, and had its head torn open by a tree branch.
The author notes that volunteering to feed the homeless and families in need peaks around November and December, and argues that energy should carry through the other 10 months.
